#9547. Pastina Soup (Italian Penicillin)

This soup is my new go-to when my family is sick. The broth here is AMAZING – light, flavorful, and nourishing. Absolute comfort food.

Published by Lindsay Ostrom on October 1, 2026

What an awesome soup recipe! The family loved it! It will be on repeat in our home especially with the kids asking for more!!! Thank you.

Like, slurp that savory broth and go back for a third bowl kind of good.

My daughter got sick last week, which means that our whole family got sick last week. And when I get sick, I lose two things: 1) my appetite, and 2) my interest in cooking.

This pastina soup truly SAVED us last week. It is:

I can’t say enough about how much I loved this last week. I sat down at the table with a steamy bowl with extra parm on top, and found myself repeatedly going back for “just one more scoop” of the broth over those tiny stars, even though I swore I hadn’t been feeling hungry just a moment earlier.

My girls were pretty excited about eating tiny star pasta with olive oil + Parmesan, while Bjork and I ladled the luscious broth over our bowls and finally tucked into some nurturing food for the first time in several days.

Pastina refers to the tiny star shaped pasta, which I found at Target, and the nickname Italian Penicillin refers to the healing nature of the savory broth – almost like a chicken noodle soup, but simpler. (And if I’m being honest, I prefer this to chicken noodle.)

I hope you are healthy and well, physically and emotionally. But if you’re not, this is comfort meal that has been serving our family so well lately!

I keep them real chunky, and I give them a quick sauté with olive oil before adding all the liquid just to get things extra fragrant.

I use water and Better Than Bouillon broth base.

Transfer to a bowl to cool down for a moment.

And then add them right back to the broth pot.

Source Notes: “Italian penicillin” is a nickname for pastina soup, or pastina (small pasta) in broth. It is playfully compared to medicine because of its healing vibe, being that it is a warm, nostalgic, nourishing comfort food. It originated with generations of Italian grandmothers and it has moved into the spotlight after becoming a popular trend on TikTok over the last few years. 🙂

5 Stars 4 Stars 3 Stars 2 Stars 1 Star

This soup has become my go-to recipe when my family is sick. The broth is amazing – simple, light, flavorful, and nourishing! It’s absolute comfort food.

Sautéing the chunky carrots, celery, onion, and garlic for 5 minutes, then simmering them in 10 cups of broth for 30 minutes before blending the vegetables with 1 to 2 cups of that broth, is a clear way to get a silky pot without cooking the pastina in it. I also like that the 1½ cups of stelline are cooked separately, drained, and tossed with a little olive oil so they don’t soak up the leftover broth overnight. If the carrot chunks are on the large side and still a bit firm at 30 minutes, do you usually just give them a few more minutes at a bare simmer, or have you found a slightly livelier bubble is fine as long as you don’t reduce the pot too far?

Is nutritional information just for broth? 1/4 dry c of the stelline pasta you recommend is 200 calories per the box. How is each serving less calories than the pasta alone? Just looking to clarify. Broth is delicious! Thanks.

I made this soup on a cold evening and blending the carrots, celery and onion into the broth gave it a much richer body than a plain clear broth, which my family noticed right away. I followed your tip to cook the pastina separately, and that kept the pasta from swelling and soaking up all the broth overnight. I used Better Than Bouillon as you suggest, and the flavor was deep without tasting overly salty, especially once I added the Parmesan at the end. I also liked the note about freezing half the broth, because I saved a batch for a busy weeknight and only had to cook fresh pastina. This comforting, simple soup is exactly the kind of recipe I reach for when someone in the house is feeling under the weather.

First kiddo went down with a GI bug last night, so I figured it was the perfect time to try this recipe! I used homemade bone broth to make the soup and added a Parmesan rind while it simmered. It’s salty, brothy, and gently flavored. We’ll see how my sick one tolerates it, but my other two kids thought it was cozy and delicious. The star pasta is a fun texture.

This is simple and delicious. I’ve made it twice now. This past time, I put the broth (sans vegetables) through a fine mesh strainer which helped get a nice and smooth texture.

Also, grocery stores near me sell relatively small carrots. I used a one-pound bag of carrots and found that to be an appropriate amount.

My son and husband woke up not feeling great this morning and I was running to Walmart anyway, so I decided to pick up the few things I needed to make a batch of this soup today!

Sadly, they didn’t have the pastina pasta, so I used bowtie pasta. I also used chicken bone broth instead of the Bouillon. And I also cooked boneless skinless chicken thighs in with the broth and veggies for some extra protein.

This was so simple and so delicious. I have a ton to freeze and a ton in the fridge for my boys to eat throughout the week as they work on feeling better.

Simply amazing! So much flavor from such simple ingredients. I’m sensitive to garlic and onions so I kept them whole to add flavor to the broth and then discarded them before blending the veggies and the soup still had so much flavor!

Is there any downside to using an immersion blender instead of taking it out and using a regular blender? Thanks!

I’ve been rocking a cold for the last 1 to 2 weeks but with pregnancy, you don’t get to take anything helpful; finally got a chance to try this, and this hot silky broth is so so good. I gave it a verrrry generous amount of fresh cracked pepper along with the grated Parmesan.

So glad you enjoyed it, and hope you feel better soon!

Very good! I had to saute longer. The only thing is when I blended, I still got a crunch from the celery.

Recently I’ve been making a version of this on repeat because I love the Progresso Chickarina soup and obsessed with the tiny star pasta but wanted a homemade version without 1000 ingredients lol!

Of course I should have checked here first! DUH! I am 100% going to blend the veggies in next time – what a great idea!

Jacquie, I am curious after reading your post if you made your own star pasta? If you did would you want to share the recipe?

Amanda, this recipe sounds so good! I can’t wait to make it!

Delicious as written! Who knew these simple ingredients could make such great soup? It reads to me like a gourmet soup starter at a fancy restaurant….

What an awesome soup recipe! The family loved it! It will be on repeat in our home especially with the kids asking for more!!! Thank you.

I couldn’t wait to try this soup. It truly did not disappoint. I used orzo because that was the smallest pasta that I had in the pantry. Will be keeping a container in my fridge for quick & healthy lunches. Thank you for the recipe.

This soup + your miracle no-knead bread is my entire personality all fall/winter long!!

Okay, now it’s ours too. Thanks for the rec!

I have made pastina before with broth bu I sure do love the extra step of blended veggies! Brillant. I will make this recipie from now on.

I’m not sick, but I couldn’t wait to make this. I had everything except celery, so I substituted a bunch of parsley (which I removed before blending) and half of a green pepper. It’s easy and so delicious and comforting, and I usually have these ingredients at home, so it will be in the regular rotation.

Thanks for making the recipe, and appreciate your notes!

LOVE Italian penicillin soup! It is a staple in our house for flu season!!

I add bell peppers into the veggies and feel like it gives an extra depth of flavor. We also do the Parmesan rind trick. I’ve always used an immersion blender and haven’t had an issue with the texture.

Made exactly as written (except used an immersion blender since it’s all I have ) and was absolutely delicious! Love how simple it is.

I don’t think I can wait for someone to get sick!

Hahaha right? Good for sick days AND regular days.

OMG, this reminds me of something my mom would make for me as a child when I was sick. Except hers used condensed cream of celery soup lol. Thanks for bringing the spirit of that dish into the 21st century so that I can share it with my son. 🙂

Cream of celery! So interesting, I’ve never heard of that in a soup like this! Love uncovering those food memories. 🙂

Hi, do you know if I can cook the Stelline directly in the broth? Looking forward to trying this recipe! Thank you!

Okay technically yes, I think you could! But here’s why I prefer not to:

– it will make the broth a bit thicker / starchier, and I prefer a silky, light broth

– the noodles will be more at risk of overcooking and getting mushy since they continue to sit in the hot liquid

– it doesn’t keep as well as leftovers (I prefer to just freeze the broth on its own)

– the experience of pouring the broth over the noodles is really fun. 🙂

Could you use an immersion mixer and keep the veggies in the bowl? Or will that change the outcome? Thank you!

I do think you could! I decided not to because I wanted it to get really silky smooth broth which I felt like my Vitamix could do better. But if you aren’t concerned about a perfectly silky smooth texture then I think it would absolutely work and it would save you the transfer!

Any thoughts about using a bone broth / regular broth blend?

Was wondering the exact same thing! My guess is it won’t get quite as smooth?

Do you really use 10 cups of broth? Does look like that much in the pictures.

Yes, 10 cups! Happens almost every time I make this that I start with 8 cups, thinking it will be enough, and then I always end up adding 2 more (at least) for a total of 10 cups to get the level of brothiness I’m looking for!

Some of it will depend on the thickness of your carrots and celery, so if you aren’t sure you could always start with 8 cups and then add to get your desired final consistency.

#9546. Apple Streusel Meal Prep Muffins

Super wholesome, loaded with streusel, and ideal for meal prep! My kids love them!

Published by Lindsay Ostrom on October 9, 2026

YUM these little meal prep apple muffins have been such a treat for my mornings!

Open windows! Crisp fall air! Hot coffee! A warm, streusely, lightly cinnamony apple muffin with tons of wholesome stuff in it and a generous pat of butter on top! It’s what I’m doing every day right now, and it’s my dream life.

The main ingredients here are shockingly basic:

I threw some brown sugar streusel on top, because streusel increases my interest in any muffin by about 500%.

I’ve been packing one of these in my girls’ lunchboxes almost every time we pack a cold lunch! I also bring them for a car snack after school pick up. My kids honestly eat one of these (or these pumpkin ones, or these zucchini ones) once a day at this point.

I don’t know that anyone cares about this, but I spend too much time thinking about these things.

5 Stars 4 Stars 3 Stars 2 Stars 1 Star

These apple streusel meal prep muffins are super wholesome, loaded with streusel, and ideal for prepping ahead! My kids love them!

Looking for some help. Mine came out really dense and kind of gummy. Maybe I over blended? Still yummy and I’ll try to make again and troubleshoot

This can happen with baked goods that only use oats. Did you let the batter sit out for a while? Baking the batter right away can sometimes help.

As expected given all your other great recipes, these were DELICIOUS and the whole family loved them! My intention was to freeze some but I don’t think they will last that long at my house. Will definitely make again!

My vitamix didn’t do a great job blending when I started with oats at the bottom. I’ll add the liquid ingredients first next time.

oh, that’s a good note – for the liquids to go first!

Just ordered the FULLSTAR chopper! Thanks for the recommendation. So much faster to get dinner ready. Smooch!~!

Easy and delicious! I made them with my toddler and we gobbled them up. I lowered the sugar to 1/2c and baked the extra batter into mini muffins that cooked in 12 minutes 🙂

These are SO GOOD and soooo nice and easy cause of blending everything. I used coconut sugar instead of brown, and gala apples instead of honeycrisp cause it’s what I had on hand, and they turned out amazing. Definitely going on the repeat list!

Thank you for yet another amazing POY recipe!! Absolutely delicious!Followed the recipe almost exactly, except I had to sub 0% Greek Yogurt for the whole milk version as that’s all I have. I ate two in a row straight out of the oven, so yummy. Can’t wait to have one with my coffee in the morning and the rest will go in the freezer for a perfect breakfast-on-the-go for my daughter who has an hour bus ride to college very early. I’ve made so many POY recipes now (made the Apple Crisp for dessert today too) they never fail, are always delicious and the whole family (fussy husband, two teens, a tween…and occasionally a 5yr old Labrador) love them.

I don’t have a Vitamix but this definitely didn’t work in my super basic blender! I ended up using my food processor with the oats first, then adding everything after. That worked great!

Oh, thank you for the notes on using the food processor! I know others were interested in using it.

Delightful little fall recipe! Not too sweet, was great w my coffee this morning. I used what apples I had on hand (gala)= 2.5 small ones. My cupcake pan holds 12, so I used my mini pan w/ the extra batter and got 16 minis too. (Cooked those for about 12 minutes along with the big ones).

I would make these again. It was a little putzsy as I only have a mini blender, so I had to blend in batches.

I swapped the oats for oat flour I already had and didn’t check my ratio so it made a few more muffins (3.5 cups oats = roughly 2.67 cups oat flour). Also added about .5 cup of oats to the topping to get an apple crisp topping.

Would love to know why you don’t recommend the Costco sprouted oats, that’s almost all we use. Love all your recipes and look forward to trying this!

Lauren, I just wanted to let you know my family made these with the Costco sprouted oats because that’s what we had on hand and we were impatient. My family still loved them and they were worth making. I’m guessing they would have been a little softer with old-fashioned rolled oats because they were maybe slightly tough, BUT it really wasn’t an issue for us.

I have applesauce on hand instead of fresh apples, would that work as a substitute?

Also curious about applesauce, if it’s getting blended already!

These are delicious! I didn’t have a full cup of Greek yogurt so I added some cottage cheese and sour cream to make 1 cup. Otherwise followed the recipe as written. Supper easy to make and everyone loved them. Will definitely make these again.

These look delicious! Can you use sour cream instead of greek yoghurt?

Could you use food processor instead of blender? Excited to try this!

I used a food processor and they came out great!

These sound delicious. You mentioned that you used brown sugar instead of maple syrup for this recipe. If I preferred to use maple syrup, what would be the recommended amount?

I haven’t tried it – I just went straight for the brown sugar to save some dollars. 🙂 And the flavor is delicious. But I would like to try it, just so we know how it works with maple syrup. I will report back when I do! (I have several muffins in this same style and they use between 1/2 cup and 3/4 cup maple syrup, but I don’t want to confirm that for this one until I know for sure.)

Lindsay said in the article that the Costco sprouted oats aren’t recommended because they absorb liquid a different way. She also said quick oats do as well and that’s why they’re not recommended either.
